column3: **Request a corrected policy-scope/conflict-surface design and reconcile the duplicate gate for the HOME-search proposal?** Concrete proposal: [role artifact contract](planned/m-fleet-role-artifact-contract.md), frozen SHA df93fee6c072bbdc19850126963049a50ff7df7cd3db13cc573a08e4fd859998. One mandatory revision completed through a quota fallback; final quorum BLOCKED (OpenAI reject, Google pass; both author vendors excluded) and independent MiniMax FAIL/N/A. Remaining premise claims compliance with every standing rule from recipe-only evidence; strict planned-doc duplicate scores1.00/0.95/0.90 remain unresolved. **A (recommended):** request corrected scope-limited policy evidence, inventory/precedence/conflict surface and duplicate-gate reconciliation; a later explicit design approval is still required before planning. **B:** leave current behavior unchanged; ticket stays open. Default if unanswered: B immediately; no planning/execution/merge. No P2 command cap or routing/quota/billing change authorized.

**`skill:idle-record-barred-on-degraded-no-pick-fire` (world, 11-09): narrow Gate 5's idle-record "degraded fire" bar? The design was blocked twice by quorum.** Measured at iteration 97: no product mission has ever promoted an idle fingerprint; World 363–370 never recorded, because every fire fell back somewhere. The bar was a fleet-controller choice (`33190af48`, iteration 91), not a ruling. [Design](planned/m-idle-record-degraded-bar.md): keep the failed-read and unfinished-gate bars, drop the lane-fallback bar, and require each candidate's only unblock event to be a dev-side OPEN ledger flip. Round 2 found two real defects: the proof block ignores the ledger parser's exit status (reproduced by the judge), and no recorded World fire would qualify, because World 370's gates are external predicates, a weekly sweep and a branch-only D-WORLD-113. **A:** one more bounded revision applying every round-2 fix (sol's exit-status capture verbatim; a retro-analysis of the last 10 World and Stapledon no-pick fires, where "do not land" is an acceptable result; a falsifiable observation criterion; a cited no-pick gate list), then one re-quorum, then plan, build and judge. **B (recommended):** no change. On the evidence, the narrowed rule would not have engaged for the mission that filed the ticket. World can make it engage on its own side by recording attended steps as rulings on dev-side ledger rows. The ticket stays open until you rule. Default if unanswered: B. Not HD-2a policy class (judge agrees); this asks because the design failed its gate, not because of policy.

**May the fleet resolve the seven open tickets whose attended fixes merged on 2026-11-16?** Measured at iteration 123: the merges are #2347 → `41c628b94` (`quorum:gpt6-1-sol-openai-api-credits-exhausted`, row 21), #2349 → `005641f82` (`pi:openrouter:uncapped-max-tokens-402`, row 50), #2348 → `509146d24` (`executor:codex-credential-collision-drops-automatic-planner-handoffs`, `executor:codex-credential-lease-collision-fails-concurrent-dispatch`, row 54; `coordinator:job-retry-success-dropped-after-failed-completion`, row 55) and #2343 → `ad2148b23` (`executor:3h-timeout-from-queue-and-unsliced-sprints`, `executor:timeout-loses-work-and-may-never-start`, row 56). All seven are still open after three days, so clause 2 keeps counting them. Iteration 115 recorded them as the attended session's claim, and the fleet has touched none. Rows 18 and 24 (config rollouts with no PR) are not included. **A**: the fleet resolves each ticket, one per fire as bookkeeping, after re-checking at HEAD that the merged fix covers the ticket's own repro, and cites the merge SHA. **B**: leave them to the attended session. **Recommendation: A**, because each has a merged, reviewed fix and the reply tells the filing mission. **Default if unanswered: B** (no change).
